Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

vow noun and verb

also make a vow, solemn promise, votive offering, pay a vow, vowed

classical

Cic. Att. 12.18.1: vōtō et prōmissō tenērī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. ND 3.93 (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 7.40.6: ejus mē compotem vōtī facere vōs potestis (Lewis & Short)

vōtum, vōtī n.

noun, second declension

a vow, a solemn promise to a god; later also a wish, a prayer

To make a vow: vōtum facere, suscipere; to pay it: vōtum solvere, reddere (Cicero). The sense “wish” is perhaps not older than Augustus’s time (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • voveō, vovēre, vōvī, vōtum — to vow, promise solemnly to a god

    verb, second conjugation · classical · Cic. ND 3.88: neque Herculī quisquam decumam vōvit umquam (Lewis & Short); Liv. 5.21.2: tibi hinc decimam partem praedae voveō (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • vōta puer solvit, quae fēmina vōverat

    as a boy he paid the vows he had made as a womanOv. Met. 9.794 (Lewis & Short)

  • tibi hinc decimam partem praedae voveō

    I vow you a tenth part of the spoil from hereLiv. 5.21.2 (Lewis & Short)

See also promise, pray, prayer.
